methodology: Reviewed every committed WebP referenced by the page inventory at its native logical viewport.
Distinguished normal below-the-fold scrolling from text or controls that are visually clipped, truncated, or crowded.
Treated blank canvas as intentional workspace, but treated a blank screenshot for a surface described as UI as an invalid capture.
Applied the Splotch design-system expectations for readable parent-facing copy, chunky controls, constrained prose measures, and responsive modal composition.

severity_scale.pass: No material responsive design problem visible in this capture.
severity_scale.low: Polish or scaling concern; content remains usable and understandable.
severity_scale.medium: Clear responsive design defect or substantial poor use of space.
severity_scale.high: Review blocker or severe defect that prevents reliable use or assessment.

priority_findings.finding: All four drawing-engine harness captures are blank, so the inventory does not actually represent that screen.
The smallest phone truncates several setting names and crowds the folder row, hiding meaning that should remain textual.
The styleguide header clips its current-page label and rests with a partially cut navigation chip on both phones.
Sparse Settings sections inherit a large fixed-height split pane and leave most of the modal blank.
The signed-out admin screen preserves a full page sheet for one shallow form, creating a large nonfunctional void.
